_meta.purpose: The controlled procedure-type vocabulary for the operative-content graph. 53 terms in 13 families. TRACKED INPUT — read by scripts/gen-opgraph.mjs; never written by it.
_meta.rule: occupancy 0 is legal ONLY with a non-empty warrant (write-invariant W3f). An empty term is not ceremony: it is the reason a later round does not force PGM logos-recitation into 'mantra-recitation'.
_meta.source: docs/plans/opgraph/PLAN.md §2.4, verbatim term list and warrants.
_meta.razor: A term names a KIND of act. It never names a step, a quantity, a duration, a formula or a sign.

terms.gloss: Recitation of a fixed formula copied verbatim in the handbook itself, as distinct from a transmitted syllable-set.
terms.warrant: Slice 11's single highest-value gap (20+ rows). The PGM's core act is reciting a logos of voces magicae and vowel chains. 'mantra-recitation' imports the wrong tradition; 'invocation-evocation' loses the fact that the formula is a fixed text copied verbatim in the handbook. Held empty at R33 because re-typing is a research act: the 16 slice-11 rows filed 'invocation/evocation' carry retypePending instead.

terms.gloss: Repeated recitation of a transmitted mantra or divine-name set within a tradition that names it as such.
Mantroddhāra — the coded derivation of a mantra from a diagram, alphabet or riddling verse.
terms.warrant: Slice 10's finding that the corpus's principal WITHHOLDING DEVICE is itself a distinct procedure and not a variety of recitation. Filing it under 'mantra-recitation' erases the fact that the text deliberately does not print the mantra.

terms.gloss: The acts by which a mantra is made operative for a particular user (saṃskāra of the mantra), as distinct from reciting it.
Non-lexical ritual sound-production — hissing, popping, vowel-chains — prescribed as an act in its own right.
terms.warrant: Slice 11: the Mithras Liturgy specifies non-lexical vocalizations alongside vowel-strings. No controlled type covers non-lexical sound-production as a ritual act, and folding it into recitation loses the distinction the text itself draws.

terms.gloss: Address to a named power to make it present, respond or appear.
The closing act by which a summoned power is released.
terms.warrant: Slice 12: dismissal must be typeable apart from invocation because ITS ABSENCE IS DIAGNOSTIC OF INCOMPLETENESS. You cannot count a missing slot you cannot name.

terms.gloss: A sworn or contractual binding between operator and power.
Regulation of breathing as a named practice.
Internally generated imagery held as the object of practice.
Contemplation with no constructed object — insight, calming, or an explicitly objectless mode.
Contemplative gazing at an EXTERNAL diagram or figure.
Systematic permutation and combination of letters as a contemplative technique (ḥokhmat ha-tseruf).
terms.warrant: Slice 14's Abulafian material. Held empty at R33 because the two works that would occupy it (jew:or-ha-sekhel, and the permutation rows of jew:hayyei-haolam-haba) are graded on source quality rather than on texts and fall below the admission floor — blocker B3. The term is declared so that a later round that obtains Bohak 2008 or Idel at page level does not file the practice under 'mantra-recitation'.

terms.gloss: A named ladder of reading, meditating, praying and contemplating a scriptural text.
terms.warrant: Guigo II's four rungs — the repo's only shipped 'complete' contemplative grade. Held empty because the only slice row that reaches for it (isl:ihya-38-muraqaba PARALLELS external:guigo-ii-scala-claustralium) was voided by audit strike E1 and Guigo II is out of this round's corpus.

terms.gloss: A held bodily posture named and required by the text.
terms.warrant: Slice 13's framing result: the famous classics mostly WITHHOLD posture (the Wuzhen pian gives no posture, no session structure, no duration). The term is declared so that a later round records the absence as an absence rather than not looking for it.

terms.gloss: A codified hand or body seal.
Placement of mantras or deities on parts of the body.
Acts making the operator, place or apparatus ritually fit.
A bounded regimen of abstention (food, drink, contact, speech) qualifying the operator for a rite.
terms.warrant: This family exists because collapsing it loses the harm signal. Folding the Abramelin ordeal, the Sar-Torah enclosure or the Mohe zhiguan's constantly-walking samādhi into 'purification' erases exactly the risk the r29 plan mandates a callout for. Held empty at R33: after razor strike R1 the Hekhalot rows are typed 'purification' with stage KINDS only, and re-typing them is a research act, not a build act.

terms.gloss: Withdrawal into a bounded retreat as the frame of a practice.
Puraścaraṇa — a counted preliminary that qualifies a mantra for use.
terms.warrant: Slice 10 names puraścaraṇa as a distinct procedure kind, but the graph may not record counts (§1.4 razor), so the term can only be occupied by a row whose evidence is structural rather than numerical. None was written this round.

terms.gloss: Construction of a geometric diagram as the object or instrument of a rite.
Construction of a mapped ritual precinct or deity-plan.
Construction of an arithmetically constrained grid (awfāq, magic squares).
terms.warrant: Slice 14's strongest proposal and the schema's most interesting case: the one row in 306 where 'complete' is a DEMONSTRABLE PROPERTY rather than a judgement — a constructed square either satisfies its magic constant or it does not, which is what engine-test.mjs already does to the seven shipped kameas. Held empty at R33 because the only rows that would occupy it sit on the awfāq→Ghāya→Agrippa chain, which blocker B1 forbids shipping.

terms.gloss: Drawing of non-alphabetic ritual signs (charaktēres, ring-letters).
terms.warrant: Slice 11: the drawn sign is a distinct medium from the spoken formula and from the diagram. Declared empty and expected to stay empty for a long time, because the graph may not record drawable signs at all (§1.4) — the term exists so the ABSENCE is typed rather than the act being mis-filed under 'yantra-construction'.

terms.gloss: Fabrication of a figure standing for a person or power.
terms.warrant: Slice 10/11: what travels in hostile rites is the STRUCTURE — the burial of the image, the naming, the substitution, the nail. Typing the effigy separately is what lets the structure be discussed without the substitution slot. Empty at R33 because every candidate row is inside the C-5 non-targeting carve-out.

terms.gloss: Construction of a bounded ritual space — circle, precinct, enclosure.
Fabrication of the instruments a rite requires (lamps, vessels, tables, seals as objects).
terms.warrant: Slice 12: the Almadel's wax table and the Ars Notoria's notae are apparatus, not talismans and not enclosures. Held empty because slice 12 explicitly refuses the circle template and the Almadel measurements, so no row can be written without measurements the razor forbids.

terms.gloss: Making an object operative by a consecrating act.
Writing and wearing (or depositing) an object with no consecration act to type.
terms.warrant: Many PGM and Coptic amulets are simply WRITTEN AND WORN, or folded and deposited — there is no consecration act, and typing them 'consecration-of-object-talisman' invents one. Empty at R33 because the applied texts that would occupy it are procedure OUTPUTS and the schema forbids grading them (W3d).

terms.gloss: An inscribed binding tablet (defixio, katadesmos) deposited in a grave, well or boundary.
terms.warrant: Slice 11: 'coercive-rite' names the intent but not the medium. An inscribed lead tablet deposited in a grave is a distinct material practice. Empty at R33 for the same C-5 reason as figurine-effigy-fabrication.

terms.gloss: Oblation into fire, or an equivalent offering act, as a named procedure.
Killing of an animal, or a blood offering, as a ritual act.
terms.warrant: 'offering-homa' is a Vedic fire-oblation term. Forcing the PGM's bird sacrifice into it erases both the act and the ethical register — and Iamblichus, De mysteriis IV–VII is an extended DEFENCE of animal sacrifice, which becomes untypeable. Empty at R33 because the two slice-11 rows that would occupy it were filed 'offering/homa' and re-typing is a research act.

terms.gloss: A procedure for obtaining an answer by a divinatory technique.
Vision sought in a reflective or translucent medium.
Casting lots whose answers are read off a fixed canonical text.
terms.warrant: Slice 13's Yijing material and slice 14's Shimmush Tehillim both operate this way, and 'divination-procedure' loses the fact that the ANSWER SET IS A BOOK. Empty at R33 because both corpora were filed with the coarse parent term and the blacklist puts the Yijing's own apparatus out of bounds for re-derivation.

terms.gloss: Sleeping in a prepared condition to obtain a dream answer.
terms.warrant: Slice 11 records dream-request recipes across the PGM. 'divination-procedure' cannot express that the operator sleeps, which is the whole procedure. Empty at R33: no row was written that names the practice without naming its preparation.

terms.gloss: Selection of a moment by astrological or calendrical rule.
An operation on substances within an alchemical frame — inner or outer.
A workshop recipe (dyeing, gilding, gem-imitation) with no ritual frame.
terms.warrant: A synthesizer keying on type names will merge two unrelated things: 'purification' in the alchemical papyri means METAL REFINING, not ritual purity. This term keeps Leiden X (111 recipes) and the Stockholm papyrus (154) out of 'alchemical-operation', whose boundary is itself the live scholarly question. Empty at R33 because slice 11 filed both papyri under 'alchemical-operation' and their genre is disputed — retyping would settle a dispute the site does not settle.

terms.gloss: Choice of substance by a correspondence rule rather than by a material property.
terms.warrant: Slice 11's Cyranides and slice 14's Picatrix both make the SELECTION the procedure. Empty at R33 because every candidate row is inside the C-1 operable-triple ceiling and no row could be written that names the rule without naming the materia.

terms.gloss: A rite of admission conferring standing or entitlement.
An ordered course of practice with named stages and a completion condition.
A rite at death or another threshold.
Codified ritual movement as a procedure.
terms.warrant: The Mevlevi samāʿ — and typing it correctly is what fixes the repo's existing misattribution of the samāʿ to the Masnavī (it was codified after Rumi's death by Sultan Walad). Empty at R33 because the correction is a domain claim carried in slice 01, not a procedure row anyone wrote.

terms.gloss: A graded ascent through named gates or ranks, structured as a liturgy.
terms.warrant: Slice 11: PGM IV.475–829 is a graded seven-stage ascent through elemental, aerial, planetary and supra-celestial ranks. A graded seven-stage ascent with named gates is not 'visualization' plus 'invocation'. Empty at R33 because both the PGM and the Hekhalot rows were filed with the coarse parents.

terms.gloss: Pratiṣṭhā — installation and consecration of an image or a building.
terms.warrant: 64 of the Īśānaśivagurudevapaddhati's 119 paṭalas. Empty at R33 because that work's rows rest partly on a wisdomlib digest of an unnamed thesis and carry '(unverified)'; the term is declared so a later round with T. Gaṇapati Śāstrī's edition in hand does not file temple consecration under 'consecration-of-object-talisman'.

terms.gloss: A rite whose declared aim is to compel, harm, drive out, immobilise or subjugate a person.
A protective rite performed ON BEHALF OF a third party.
terms.warrant: Filing the Netratantra's court priest acting FOR THE MONARCH, or Kauśika's śāntika/pauṣṭika, under 'purification' erases the ON-BEHALF-OF relation, which is the ethically salient fact. Empty at R33 because slice 10 filed those rows under 'purification' and 'coercive-rite' and retyping requires re-reading the source.

terms.gloss: A second-order table of ritual VARIABLES that contains no discrete rite.
terms.warrant: THE MOST IMPORTANT TERM IN THE LIST. Ullrey (UCSB 2016, pp. 117–142): Mantramahodadhi 25, Śāradātilaka 23.121–45 and Prapañcasāra 446–452 contain no discrete rites — 'no discrete rituals are found in this section'; 'a second-order text cannot describe a first-order text.' Without it the corpus's two most-cited operative chapters are unfilable, and the repo's abhicāra wing looks timid when it is in fact FAITHFUL: its refusal to assemble the nineteen variables is fidelity, because the source chapter has nothing to assemble. Declared empty at R33 because slice 10 filed those rows under 'coercive-rite' and 'mantra-consecration'; A LATER ROUND MUST NOT 'COMPLETE' THEM.

terms.gloss: A work that discusses, classifies and justifies ritual at length and contains no executable sequence.
terms.warrant: The role slice 11 needed for De mysteriis, Proclus' On the Hieratic Art and Porphyry's Letter to Anebo. Without it the graph either falsely credits them with procedures or falsely records them as procedure-free. At R33 the distinction is carried by the work-level role 'meta-procedural' instead, so the type stays empty — the term is kept because role and type answer different questions.

terms.gloss: Procedure-shaped material that is in fact a cipher or concealment system.
A record of sessions performed, from which a procedure can be reconstructed but which is not itself a manual.
